questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

From 1990 to 2000 each of the countries listed below changed towards a market economy through privatisation programmes. private sector share (% of GDP) (ratio of private enterprise earnings to GDP) 1990 1995 2000 Czechia 10 70 80 Hungary 20 60 80 Romania 15 45 60 Slovakia 10 60 80 What can be concluded about the rates of privatisation?

options.A: Czechia initially made the fastest change.
options.B: Hungary made the least overall change.
options.C: Romania made the greatest overall change.
options.D: Slovakia made the steadiest change.

questions.questionText: Farmers using traditional methods lack access to finance and often employ family members on a part-time basis. If working practices in agriculture could be improved, how would this be likely to be shown on the production possibility curve? R manufactured goods T S O agricultural goods

options.A: by a movement from R to T
options.B: by a movement from S to R
options.C: by a movement from S to T
options.D: by a movement from T to R

questions.questionText: Which types of good are distinguished from one another by the presence or absence of opportunity cost?

options.A: demerit and merit goods
options.B: economic and free goods
options.C: inferior goods and normal goods
options.D: private and public goods

questions.questionText: What could cause a shift in the supply curve of good X and a movement along its supply curve? shift in the supply curve movement along the supply curve

options.A: a change in consumer preferences an increase in the price of a substitute good
options.B: a decrease in factor productivity the imposition of a tax on good X
options.C: an increase in the price of a an increase in factor productivity complementary good
options.D: an increase in the wage rates a change in consumer preferences in the industry

questions.questionText: A supply curve is represented by the equation, quantity supplied = 10 + 5P, where P = the price of the product. Which price rise would cause the quantity supplied to double?

options.A: $1 to $2 B $1 to $3 C $1 to $4 D $1 to $5

questions.questionText: Along which axis can the market demand curve be aggregated from individual demand curves?

options.A: both the horizontal and vertical axis
options.B: the horizontal axis only
options.C: the horizontal or the vertical axis but not both
options.D: the vertical axis only

questions.questionText: The table shows the price of a good and total expenditure on the good during specific periods when the market is in equilibrium. price total expenditure period ($) ($)

The Chinese government relaxed controls on private house ownership. Private house ownership rose sharply, replacing demand for apartments rented from the state. What would have been most likely to happen to private house prices and the rents of apartments? private house prices apartment rents

options.A: decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: What might explain a simultaneous increase in both price and quantity traded in the market for a normal good?

options.A: the removal of an effective maximum price on the good
options.B: technological progress in the production of the good
options.C: the imposition of a tax on the good
options.D: the granting of a subsidy to producers of the good

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand and supply curves for parking spaces in a hospital car park. S price P D O number of spaces The managers decide to rely on the price mechanism to allocate parking spaces at the hospital. What is required for this to work?

options.A: Alternative means of transport must be provided for those unable to afford price OP.
options.B: A survey will be needed to find out the amount users are willing to pay.
options.C: The capacity of the car park will need to be expanded.
options.D: The price charged for parking spaces must be OP.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a market for a good which is supplied partly from domestic production and partly from imports. S represents domestic supply and S represents imports. h m S h price S m D O R T V quantity What will be the level of consumption and the associated quantity of imports? consumption quantity of imports

options.A: OT RT
options.B: OT OT
options.C: OV RT
options.D: OV RV

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for computers in Pakistan. W supply price Y X demand O Z quantity Which areas represent consumer surplus and consumer expenditure? consumer consumer surplus expenditure

options.A: WXY OXY
options.B: WXY OXYZ
options.C: WYO OXYZ
options.D: WYO OYZ

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for labour. At which level would an effective minimum wage rate have to be set? labour supply wage A rate B C

options.D: labour demand O quantity of labour employed

questions.questionText: What is an accurate statement about a production subsidy?

options.A: It causes demand for the good to increase so the demand curve shifts to the right.
options.B: It enables firms to supply more so the supply curve shifts to the left.
options.C: It is financial assistance to firms from the government to help increase output.
options.D: It is money taken from firms by the government to reduce harmful side effects of production.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market supply and demand curves for an agricultural product. The government guarantees producers a price of at least OX for their output, but allows the market price to be freely determined by demand and supply. supply price U X Y Z V W demand O S T quantity Which area in the diagram represents the total subsidy payments made by the government to producers?

options.A: UYTS B UYZW C XUWV D XYZV

questions.questionText: How will transfer payments to low-income families, funded by a mix of direct taxation and indirect taxation, affect the total level of consumption?

options.A: The change in the level will be uncertain.
options.B: The level will fall.
options.C: The level will remain unchanged.
options.D: The level will rise.

questions.questionText: The table shows the annual percentage change in the output per worker employed for four nationalised industries before and after privatisation. nationalised before after industry privatisation privatisation railways –4% 2% electricity supply 7% 9% shipbuilding 4% –1% telecommunications 6% 6% What can be concluded from the table about the effect of privatisation?

options.A: Employment fell in the railway industry.
options.B: Employment was unchanged in the telecommunications industry.
options.C: Output was greatest in the electricity supply industry.
options.D: Workers became less efficient in the shipbuilding industry.

questions.questionText: In its recent budget a government increased defence expenditure and the amount spent on training to increase the productivity of the workforce. The initial equilibrium point is shown by X on the aggregate demand, AD, and aggregate supply, AS, diagram. What would be the equilibrium point after these changes? AS AS B price level AS X A C D AD AD AD

The table shows a country’s consumer price index for March and April 2015. consumer price index March 2015 151.3 April 2015 148.6 Which statement correctly describes what happened between these two months?

options.A: There was a decrease in the annual rate of inflation.
options.B: There was a decrease in real interest rates.
options.C: There was an increase in the purchasing power of money.
options.D: There was an increase in the standard of living.

questions.questionText: What would be likely to increase inflation in an economy?

options.A: an increase in consumer saving
options.B: an increase in interest rates
options.C: an increase in labour productivity
options.D: an increase in taxes on imports

questions.questionText: In 2014 a rich foreign businessman bought a UK football club. What would have been the immediate effect of such an investment?

options.A: a fall in the demand for footballers in the UK
options.B: a fall in the earnings of footballers in the UK
options.C: an inflow in the UK balance of payments
options.D: an inflow in the UK balance of trade

questions.questionText: Australia’s spending on imports falls and, at the same time, investment abroad by Australian firms declines. Which diagram shows the immediate effect of these changes on the market for the Australian dollar?

options.A: B price of D price of S S D 1 Australian D Australian S dollars dollars P P 1 P P D S

questions.questionText: An economy’s terms of trade rose from the base year of 100 to 110. Which changes in the export price index and the import price index would have caused this? export price import price index change index change
The introduction of the euro as the common currency of much of Western Europe created a powerful economic group. What is least likely to have been the intention?

options.A: faster economic growth in the region
options.B: greater labour mobility and employment in the region
options.C: more international trade within the region
options.D: more international trade with non-members

questions.questionText: Country X has a comparative advantage in producing wheat and country Y in producing cars. However, the countries choose not to specialise and trade. What is a valid reason for this behaviour?

options.A: The cost of transport is high relative to the opportunity cost differences between the countries.
options.B: The exchange rate lies within the countries’ opportunity cost ratios.
options.C: There is immobility of factors of production between the countries.
options.D: Trade is based on absolute rather than comparative advantage.

questions.questionText: What is not an example of protectionism?

options.A: a ban on the imports of chicken products
options.B: import tariffs on agricultural products
options.C: maximum supermarket food prices
options.D: strict health and safety requirements

questions.questionText: The government of a country plans to cut income tax rates. The initial equilibrium for the country is represented by point X on the diagram. Which new equilibrium point would an economist predict as the result? AS price A AS level 1 B D X C AD AD AD O real national income
If an economy has a floating exchange rate, which policy could have an expansionary effect on national income with the smallest reduction of a current account surplus on the balance of payments?

options.A: a reduction in income tax rates
options.B: a reduction in interest rates
options.C: government subsidies to individuals wanting loans for house purchases
options.D: increased government spending on transport infrastructure

questions.questionText: Which combination of fiscal and monetary policies is most likely to be effective in the short run for tackling deflation in a closed economy? fiscal policy monetary policy

options.A: increasing the budget deficit reducing the interest rate
options.B: increasing the budget deficit reducing the money supply
options.C: reducing the budget deficit reducing the interest rate
